description:
Which verifier: one fact_id → verify_fact_lineage; a list of fact_ids or derived_ids → verify_facts; a number with no id → match_derived; a number quoted from filing text or insider/13F rows → verify_filing_figures; every number in a saved report → verify_report_figures; figures a later filing revised → check_report_figures_current.

Resolve MANY cited facts to their SEC filings in ONE call — the batch form of `verify_fact_lineage`. Use this whenever you are checking a LIST of figures rather than a single number: reviewing a report's citations, auditing a thesis's evidence, or confirming every figure in a draft before you sign it. A 30-figure report is one call here and 30 calls with `verify_fact_lineage`.

Use `verify_fact_lineage` INSTEAD when you have one figure, or when you do not have a fact_id and need the concept-name lookup (`concept` + `as_of_date`) — this tool resolves by fact_id only.

A MISS IS DATA, NOT A FAILURE: each item comes back `found:true` with its full `lineage`, or `found:false` with an error `code` and `message`. One unresolvable fact_id never costs you the other verdicts, so read every item — `summary` gives you requested / found / missing at a glance.

Duplicate (ticker, fact_id) pairs are collapsed before anything is read, so `summary.requested` counts UNIQUE pairs and may be lower than the number of entries you sent; results come back in first-seen order. Maximum 50 facts per call.

Never state a figure this tool returned `found:false` for, and never fabricate a lineage it did not return. Available on all plans; each fact is subject to the same tier reach as `verify_fact_lineage`.

DERIVED FIGURES: an item may be `{ derived_id }` instead of `{ ticker, fact_id }`. A figure a Valuein tool computed (a margin, a growth rate, free cash flow) carries a `derived_id`; this tool re-reads its input facts from the filings, re-runs the registered formula and returns the recomputed `lineage.display` plus a `derived` block listing the inputs. Compare `lineage.display` to the figure you stated. A derived item is `found:false` with UNKNOWN_FORMULA, INPUT_NOT_FOUND (incl. an input not yet accepted at `as_of_date`), INPUT_UNAVAILABLE, UNDEFINED_RESULT, INVALID_ARGUMENT or ENTITLEMENT_DENIED when it cannot be proven (permanent), or UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE / STALE_SNAPSHOT / RATE_LIMITED when the read failed (transient, retry). At most 5 distinct companies across derived items per call; chunk larger sets. `as_of_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) applies the point-in-time cut to every derived input.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cut (YYYY-MM-DD) for `derived_id` items: an input whose filing was accepted after this date is INPUT_NOT_FOUND. Fact items are unaffected.

facts.description: The facts to verify, 1–50 of them. Group a report's whole citation list here rather than calling once per figure. Duplicate (ticker, fact_id) pairs are resolved once and returned once, in first-seen order.

fact_id.description: Deterministic fact identity hash: SHA-256(entity_id|accession_id|concept|period_end|unit), 64-char lowercase hex, exactly as a previous tool result gave it to you. Never invent one.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK.B — or a CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. '0000320193'. The company the fact belongs to; a fact_id is only resolvable against its own filer.

derived_id.description: Citation id of a figure the server computed (`drv1:<cik>:<formula>@<v>:<role>=<fact_id>,...`), exactly as a tool result gave it to you. It is re-derived from its input facts. Never invent one.

name: verify_facts

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).

results.description: One entry per UNIQUE requested pair, in first-seen order. Check `found` before reading `lineage`.

derived.description: Present on a re-derived (`drv1:`) item: the formula and the input facts the engine re-read. `lineage.display` is the engine's recomputed figure.

formula_id.description: The registered formula that was re-run, e.g. margin.gross@1.

inputs.description: The facts the figure was recomputed from; empty for a pipeline-computed ratio.

fact_id.description: The source fact that filled the role.

role.description: The role this input plays in the formula.

derived_id.description: Set when this item was a `drv1:` derived id (echoed).

fact_id.description: The fact_id this item asked about — echoed so a caller can key results without relying on order.

found.description: The fact resolved; `lineage` carries its full provenance chain.

lineage.description: Full provenance for one fact. Identity: fact_id, entity_id, ticker, company_name, concept, standard_concept, accession_id. Value: numeric_value (raw), `display` (the SAME number already rendered — "$391.04B" — QUOTE THIS rather than re-rounding numeric_value yourself), unit, plus derived_quarterly_value/derived_quarterly_display/derived_quarterly_label (the standalone quarter: a Q2/Q3 10-Q states year-to-date and a 10-K the whole year, so the quarter and the filing are different numbers). Filing: source_url, inline_viewer_url, document_url, filing_date, form_type, accepted_at. Duration: period_start, period_end, period_span_days, and period_type (instant | quarterly | half_year | nine_month | annual | duration) so a 3-month stub is never mistaken for the 12-month figure — a 10-K tags BOTH at the same period_end. ⚠️ There is no `value` key and no `cik` key; the fields are named exactly as emitted.

accepted_at.description: SEC acceptance timestamp (ISO 8601) — the moment this number became public. The PIT cut is taken on this.

accession_id.description: SEC accession number of the filing that reported this value, e.g. 0000320193-24-000123.

concept.description: Raw XBRL tag as the filer used it, e.g. us-gaap:Revenues.

derived_quarterly_display.description: `derived_quarterly_value` rendered the same way. Null when that value is null.

derived_quarterly_label.description: Present whenever `derived_quarterly_value` is: says which standalone quarter it is (a Q4 split off a 10-K, or a Q2/Q3 split off a year-to-date 10-Q). It is never the figure in `display`.

derived_quarterly_value.description: The three-month figure derived from a year-to-date filing. A Q2/Q3 10-Q states YTD, so THIS and `numeric_value` are different numbers for the same fact — a verifier comparing against whichever one it happened to read passes wrong numbers half the time. Null when no derivation applies.

display.description: `numeric_value` ALREADY RENDERED — "$391.04B", "$6.11". QUOTE THIS character-for-character rather than re-rounding `numeric_value` yourself: the rendering also needs a scale, and `unit` alone cannot tell a fraction (0.5965 → "59.65%") from a percent (0.5965 → "0.60%"). Null when `numeric_value` is null.

document_url.description: Direct link to the rendered primary document (not the index page). Null when the primary document is unknown.

entity_id.description: Zero-padded 10-digit SEC CIK of the filer. (The key is named entity_id — there is no `cik` field.)

filing_date.description: Filing date (YYYY-MM-DD). Null when the filing join found nothing.

form_type.description: Filing form type — 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F. Null when the filing join found nothing.

inline_viewer_url.description: SEC Inline-XBRL viewer opened on the rendered primary document — the strongest one-click verification link. Null when the filing is not Inline-XBRL or the primary document is unknown.

numeric_value.description: The raw reported value. Null when the fact carries no numeric value.

period_end.description: End of the reporting window (YYYY-MM-DD), or the instant date for balance-sheet facts.

period_span_days.description: Length of the reporting window in days. Null when not derivable.

period_start.description: Start of the reporting window (YYYY-MM-DD). Null for instant (balance-sheet) facts.

period_type.description: Coarse duration class: instant | quarterly | half_year | nine_month | annual | duration. A single 10-K tags BOTH a 12-month figure and a 3-month Q4 stub at the same period_end, so this is what stops a stub being quoted as the annual number.

source_url.description: SEC filing-index URL. Null when the filing join found nothing.

standard_concept.description: Valuein's standardized concept name (TotalRevenue, NetIncome, …); null when the raw tag is unmapped.

ticker.description: The company's uppercase ticker: the one you passed, or for a lookup by CIK its listed symbol (the CIK itself only for a registrant with no listed security).

unit.description: Unit of the value, e.g. USD, USD/share, shares.

ticker.description: The uppercased ticker (or CIK) this item asked about.

derived_id.description: Set when this item was a `drv1:` derived id (echoed).

error.description: Why this item could not be resolved. Never fabricate a lineage for an item that carries this.

code.description: Machine-readable reason: TICKER_NOT_FOUND (the company is outside the bucket your plan reads), DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE_FOR_PERIOD (the period is outside your history window, or no fact carries that fact_id for that company), or any other code the lookup raised — the original code is preserved, never flattened. Derived items add INVALID_ARGUMENT, UNKNOWN_FORMULA, INPUT_NOT_FOUND, INPUT_UNAVAILABLE, UNDEFINED_RESULT and ENTITLEMENT_DENIED (permanent: a human must act) and pass the data layer's transient codes through unchanged (UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, STALE_SNAPSHOT, RATE_LIMITED, INTERNAL_ERROR: retry).

fact_id.description: The fact_id this item asked about.

found.description: This one fact could not be resolved. The other items in the call are unaffected — read them.

ticker.description: The uppercased ticker (or CIK) this item asked about.

summary.description: Counts over `results`. Quote `missing` when reporting coverage — it is the number of figures you could NOT tie to a filing.

found.description: How many resolved to a filing.

missing.description: How many did not. Always `requested - found`; a non-zero value is a fact about your citations, not about this call.

requested.description: Unique (ticker, fact_id) pairs resolved — duplicates in your input are collapsed.

title: Verify Facts (batch)
